hero.desc: Senior scientist and associate researcher at the Rattan Lal Center for Carbon Management at The Ohio State University — a world reference in soil organic carbon dynamics, the No-Till System, and regenerative agriculture in the tropics.

welcomeModal.title: Welcome to our knowledge space!
welcomeModal.p1: It is with great joy that I start this blog to share the knowledge accumulated over 45 years dedicated to soil science. In this journey, I understood a great truth: the more experience we gain, the more questions arise and the more we need to evolve.
welcomeModal.p2: We are in constant transformation. In an era where information floods the internet and leaves us confused, filtering what truly works is our greatest challenge. After all, there is no single recipe in agriculture: for each climate, terrain, soil and management, there are specific practices. Our role is to know how to choose the best one.
welcomeModal.subtitle1: The Agricultural Revolution and the Future of Soil
welcomeModal.p3: Over the last five decades, the No-Till System (NTS) has established itself as the greatest revolution in Brazilian agriculture. It reduced erosion, improved soil health, and brought resilience, generating more productivity and profitability for farmers. But its greatest legacy is social: ensuring fertile and productive soil for future generations.
welcomeModal.p4: After years of study and practice, I am absolutely convinced of a crucial factor: the success of NTS depends on the efficient management of soil organic matter. It is the one that controls the physical, chemical, and biological attributes of the soil.
welcomeModal.p5: I start this new challenge with enthusiasm, simplicity, and an open spirit. I invite you to explore with us the management of soil organic matter and its interactions, towards healthy, resilient, productive, profitable, and low CO₂ emission production systems.

courseModal.title: Transform the Field: Discover the Science Behind Carbon Agriculture
courseModal.p1: Knowledge is our greatest treasure. It is what transforms theory into real, safe productivity in the field.
courseModal.p2: After nearly 30 years of continuous research, trials, successes, and many collaborations, the time has come to share this legacy with you. We are proud to launch the course: "Carbon management for healthy, resilient, profitable, and low CO₂ emission production systems".
courseModal.sub1: Why is this course important for you?
courseModal.p3: Today, terms like carbon credits, net zero, and environmental services have become mantras in the agricultural sector. But what do they mean in practice?
courseModal.p4: As a scientist, I understand that science only fulfills its role when it leaves the laboratories and produces results in everyday farming. There is no successful practice without a solid theory. This course was designed to give you the independence and confidence needed to apply these concepts wisely, adapting them to your reality.
courseModal.p5: The training is completely free and divided into 5 weekly modules. Each week, we release a new step in your journey:
courseModal.module1: Module 1 – Carbon Agriculture (Available now): Introduction and the pillars of Carbon Agriculture.
courseModal.module2to5: Modules 2 to 5: Management techniques, soil resilience, profitability and carbon markets (weekly releases).
courseModal.p6: Watch the lessons, absorb the content, and make the most of this material made for your growth.

perfil.bio1:
Prof. Juca Sá is one of the world's leading experts in soil organic carbon dynamics in No-Till systems. His scientific journey began in 1981, shortly after graduating in Agronomic Engineering from UFRRJ, passing through pioneering No-Till institutions such as Fundação ABC, UEPG (State University of Ponta Grossa) — where he worked from 1996 to 2019 — and today as a senior associate researcher at The Ohio State University, alongside Nobel Peace Prize laureate Prof. Rattan Lal.

His research has demonstrated that No-Till, when correctly implemented across its three pillars, can restore soil organic carbon stocks to levels comparable to native vegetation. A 2025 study co-authored with Rattan Lal — covering 63 farms across the Cerrado and Atlantic Forest biomes — confirmed that 25% of properties already exceed carbon stocks of native vegetation.

He has mentored 32 undergraduate students, 12 master's, 3 doctoral, and 7 post-doctoral researchers, and trained researchers from 11 countries across Asia and Africa in 7 editions of international courses on soil organic matter management.

timeline.text: B.Sc. in Agronomic Engineering — Federal Rural University of Rio de Janeiro. Began career at the Dairy Farmers Cooperative of Paraná.
Soil fertility researcher — Fundação ABC, a pioneering No-Till institution in Brazil. First deep engagement with the NT system.
M.Sc. (UFPR) and Ph.D. in Soils — ESALQ/USP with a sandwich period at The Ohio State University. First international publications on carbon sequestration in Brazilian Oxisols.
Associate Professor C — Dept. of Soil Science and Agricultural Engineering, UEPG. Built one of Brazil's leading research groups in soil organic matter.
Post-doctorates (2008, 2012) and Senior Visiting Professor (2015) at C-MASC (Carbon Management and Sequestration Center), alongside Prof. Rattan Lal.
Opening speaker at the House of Sustainable Agriculture — presented groundbreaking NT carbon sequestration results at the UN COP30.

opinioes.title: The 3 Pillars of the No-Till System
opinioes.lead: According to Prof. Juca Sá, 85–90% of "no-till" areas in Brazil do not correctly apply the three fundamental principles — and this compromises all the benefits of the system.

principios.descricao: The soil is disturbed only at the seeding row. No conventional plowing or harrowing. The natural structure and soil aggregates are preserved.
Living plants or straw throughout the year. Requires 16–19 t/ha of biomass/straw to ensure continuous protection and feed soil biota year-round.
Diversity of plant species in rotation to increase quality and quantity of biomass-C, stimulate edaphic biota, and break pest and disease cycles.

citacoes.texto: Crop residues are the food of the soil, and by feeding the soil, we feed humans — and agriculture can contribute to minimizing the climate crisis.
